verified_title: STARRY: Spatial-Temporal Action-Centric World Modeling for Robotic Manipulation
problem: Appearance-only future modeling can miss the metric geometry of grasps, handovers and placement. Generic token attention need not emphasize regions near the end-effector.
contribution: Joint spatial-temporal world/action denoising with an explicit future-depth/EE geometry expert and Geometry-Aware Selective Attention Modulation (GASAM) applied only to action-to-video attention.
algorithm: Compose calibrated multiview RGB-D and projected historical EE trajectories into a shared layout. Wan-based world and action experts jointly denoise future latents/actions while Qwen-VL supplies semantics. A geometry expert predicts depth/EE positions; unproject depth into metric3D, compute distances, map them monotonically to weights and add weighted log-bias to action attention. Train flow objectives plus depth, pose and geometric-weight losses.
observations: Three calibrated RGB-D views, camera parameters, current pose, EE/action history and language. A single RGB overview does not satisfy this sensor contract, and predicted geometry must retain its provenance.
actions: 14D state/action configuration with16-step chunks,8 predicted video frames and10 denoising steps. Robot-specific control semantics remain required; attention modulation does not enforce kinematics or contact forces.
embodiment_and_data: Hierarchical web, human, simulation, geometry and multi-robot data, then RoboTwin50tasks with50 clean and500 randomized demos/task. Physical ARXR5 uses3tasks with50 demos/task. Appendix specifies8A100-80G workers, roughly one week for40kstep/batch256 fine-tuning; pretraining scales to more workers.
experiments: RoboTwin clean/randomized joint training for40ksteps and crossed representation/GASAM ablations. Physical handover vegetables, tidying a box and shaking/placing a bottle:20 rollouts/task/method, scored at nested stages. Stage2 builds on stage1; six percentages are not six independent datasets.
baselines: pi0.5, X-VLA, Motus and LingBot-VA, with GO-1/pi0 in the appendix. Controlled ablation crosses action-only, appearance-only and full spatial-temporal prediction with modulation enabled/disabled. Geometry inputs and pretraining are not uniformly matched across published baselines.
limitations: Depth/EE prediction errors can misdirect attention; spatial saliency does not guarantee forces or collision behavior. Exact distance kernel/modulation choices and depth-failure handling need source verification. Three RGB-D views and A100 resources differ substantially from Pi C920. Three two-stage rigid-object tasks establish no cloth/sock result or NX latency.
code_and_license: No source commit, weights, license files or dataset terms audited; no execution. Backbone citations supply no independent license evidence.
hardware_adaptation: COMPARE geometry-informed attention offline with available Nano RGB-D only after verifying intrinsics, extrinsics and metric depth. Pi RGB cannot silently replace three RGB-D views. Preserve actual frame/state provenance, separately tag predicted depth and map the14D schema to the calibrated target. Existing controller settings remain unchanged.
